therapeutic_hypothesis.compound: Insulin Lispro Protamine Suspension vs Insulin Glargine
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: Adults with type 2 diabetes on anti-hyperglycemic medications
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Change from baseline to 24-week endpoint in HbA1c

results.effect_size: Mean difference (lispro - glargine) = -0.05% HbA1c (95% CI: -0.21 to 0.11)
biomarker_changes: HbA1c decreased from ~8.70% at baseline to ~7.15% (lispro) and ~7.24% (glargine) at 24 weeks
Daily mean 7-point SMBG: 7.79 mmol/L (lispro) vs 7.96 mmol/L (glargine) at endpoint
Glycemic variability (SD of fasting BG): 1.01 mmol/L (lispro) vs 0.94 mmol/L (glargine), p=0.323
subgroup_findings: Nocturnal hypoglycemia: 114 vs 87 participants (lispro vs glargine), p=0.011
Severe hypoglycemia: 9 vs 2 participants (lispro vs glargine), p=0.036
1-year adjusted nocturnal hypoglycemic rate: 6.08 vs 4.08 events/year (lispro vs glargine), p<0.001
Total daily insulin dose higher with lispro (33.28 U) vs glargine (30.85 U), p=0.031
safety_signals: Higher rate of nocturnal hypoglycemia with insulin lispro protamine suspension vs insulin glargine (p=0.011)
Higher rate of severe hypoglycemia with insulin lispro protamine suspension vs insulin glargine (p=0.036)
1-year adjusted nocturnal hypoglycemic rate significantly higher with lispro (6.08 vs 4.08, p<0.001)
Serious adverse events were infrequent and balanced between arms

dose_info.schedule: Once daily (QD) or twice daily (BID) for lispro; once daily (QD) for glargine; subcutaneous injection x 24 weeks

results_by_chain.endpoint: HbA1c change from baseline at 24 weeks
results_by_chain.population_description: Adults with type 2 diabetes on anti-hyperglycemic medications
